place.source_title: Mazeppa Ancient Order of United Workmen Building, First Street

brief: Two-storey red-brick commercial block and lodge hall built in 1912 by the local AOUW lodge (founded 1878) in a small Zumbro River village: two storefronts with wood-framed display windows and transoms under a continuous cornice, paired 1/1 upper windows with stone sills lighting the lodge hall, recessed brick panels, a corbelled cornice and a raised central parapet ornament. Several upper sashes are broken; a frame house and a metal shed flank it.

facade.notes: the AOUW lodge building (Mazeppa MN, 1912): a two-storey brick block with a bracketed metal cornice and a pediment-name plate, upper windows broken (the lodge hall), a ground floor of old storefronts and doors partly boarded; a semi trailer parked at the curb

why.note: the two-part block: shop below, lodge hall or flats above
a fading village main street: the lodge hall empty above
